context: Telephone call to book a place at a dog boarding kennels

cues.t: Part 1. You will hear a woman telephoning a boarding kennels to book a place for her dog. First you have some time to look at questions 1 to 10.
You will see that there is an example that has been done for you. On this occasion only, the conversation relating to this will be played first.
Hillcrest Boarding Kennels, Gareth speaking.
Good morning. We're going on holiday this summer, and I'd like to book a place for my dog.
Of course. Can I start with your name?
Yes, it's Mrs Ashworth. A-S-H-W-O-R-T-H.

The woman's surname is Ashworth, so Ashworth has been written in the space. Now we shall begin. You should answer the questions as you listen, because you will not hear the recording a second time. Listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 10.
Hillcrest Boarding Kennels, Gareth speaking.
Good morning. We're going on holiday this summer, and I'd like to book a place for my dog.
Of course. Can I start with your name?
Yes, it's Mrs Ashworth. A-S-H-W-O-R-T-H.
Thank you, Mrs Ashworth. And what's your dog called?
Our last dog was called Rusty, and I still use that name by mistake sometimes. But this one is Pepper, because of the little black spots on his nose.
That's a nice name. What breed is he?
People always think he's a beagle, because of his colouring, but he's actually a spaniel.
Lovely dogs. And how old is he?
We've had him for seven years, but he was two when we got him, so he's 9 now.
He's still got plenty of energy, then?
Oh yes. He'll walk for hours if you let him, though he does get a bit stiff in cold weather.
We walk all our dogs twice a day, and there's a big field behind the kennels where they can run around.
Right. And when would you like him to come to us?
Our flight is on the 19th of July, but it leaves very early in the morning, so I'd like to bring him the day before, on the 18th.
Let me check the calendar. Yes, we've got space then. How long will he be staying?
Ten nights altogether. We're going to visit my sister in Canada.
That's fine. Now, our prices depend on size. It's 22 pounds a night for small dogs, 28 pounds for medium dogs, and 35 pounds for large ones.
He's definitely medium.
So that'll be 28 pounds a night, including his food and exercise.
That's reasonable. Now, I should mention his health. He used to have problems with his ears, but they're fine now. The important thing is that he has to take a tablet every morning for his heart.
Our staff are used to that. Just give us the tablets in the original packet. What about his diet?
Tinned food gives him a terrible stomach upset, so he only eats dry food. I'll bring a bag of the brand he likes.
How much does he usually have?
Two small bowls a day, one in the morning and one in the early evening. I'll write it all down for you.
Thanks, that's very helpful. We like to keep to the same routine they have at home.
No problem. Many owners like to bring something from home, to help their dogs settle in. We can't accept toys, because the dogs fight over them, but a blanket is ideal.
He's got an old one that he sleeps on, so I'll bring that.
That'll be a comfort to him, especially at night. Does he get on with other dogs?
He's very friendly, but he's a little nervous of big dogs.
Then we'll put him in a quiet area, next to some of the smaller ones.
Perfect. There's one document we'll need to see. We don't ask for your insurance details, but you must bring his vaccination certificate, or we can't accept him.
I'll make sure I find it. Now, we get home on a Sunday afternoon, so could I come straight from the airport to pick him up?

I'm sorry, but that won't be possible. We're open on Saturday mornings, but dogs can't be collected on a Sunday, because there's only one member of staff on duty. You could come first thing on the Monday.
All right, we'll do that. Thank you very much.
You're welcome. I'll put a confirmation in the post today, with a map showing how to find us.
That would be useful. We've never been up to your part of the valley before.
It's easy enough. Just look out for the large green sign at the end of the lane.
That is the end of Part 1. You now have half a minute to check your answers.
